title: Downloading AgERA5 data with ag5Tools
text: Copernicus “Agrometeorological indicators 1979 present derived reanalysis” dataset (AgERA5) provides daily surface meteorological data 0.1° (~11 km) resolution 1979 present. ag5_download() function gives programmatic access dataset R via Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS) API. downloaded file covers one day one variable, stored NetCDF (.nc) file. Across full year means 365 (366) files per variable, one per day.

title: Downloading AgERA5 data with ag5Tools
text: Create free account https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu.

title: Downloading AgERA5 data with ag5Tools
text: logging , API key shown profile page. Follow instructions CDS API Guide create .cdsapirc configuration file home directory containing key.

title: Downloading AgERA5 data with ag5Tools
text: ag5Tools calls CDS via Python cdsapi library using reticulate package. Python cdsapi installed, ag5_download() install automatically first use.

title: Downloading AgERA5 data with ag5Tools
text: ag5_download() uses CDS API variable names (snake_case). differ file names written disk, used ag5_extract(). See vignette("extracing_data") mapping two naming systems.

title: Downloading AgERA5 data with ag5Tools
text: variables available multiple daily statistics. Provide statistic name statistic argument. 2m_temperature — must specify one : 10m_wind_speed, vapour_pressure, cloud_cover, 2m_dewpoint_temperature — 24_hour_mean available. statistic argument must provided. precipitation_flux, solar_radiation_flux, snow_thickness, snow_thickness_lwe, liquid_precipitation_duration_fraction, solid_precipitation_duration_fraction — statistic argument needed. 2m_relative_humidity — statistic, requires time argument: "06_00", "09_00", "12_00", "15_00", "18_00".

title: Downloading AgERA5 data with ag5Tools
code: library(ag5Tools)  ag5_download(   variable  = "2m_temperature",   statistic = "24_hour_maximum",   year      = 2015,   month     = 6,   day       = 15,   path      = "C:/agera5_data" )

title: Downloading AgERA5 data with ag5Tools
text: Set day = "" download every day specified month.
code: ag5_download(   variable  = "precipitation_flux",   year      = 2015,   month     = 6,   day       = "all",   path      = "C:/agera5_data" )

title: Downloading AgERA5 data with ag5Tools
text: Set month = "" day = "" download full year.
code: ag5_download(   variable  = "solar_radiation_flux",   year      = 2020,   month     = "all",   day       = "all",   path      = "C:/agera5_data" )

title: Downloading AgERA5 data with ag5Tools
code: ag5_download(   variable = "2m_relative_humidity",   time     = "09_00",   year     = 2015,   month    = "all",   day      = "all",   path     = "C:/agera5_data" )

title: Downloading AgERA5 data with ag5Tools
text: default ag5_download() downloads full global extent. Use area argument restrict download region interest — substantially reduces file size download time.

title: Downloading AgERA5 data with ag5Tools
text: Provide numeric vector c(north, west, south, east) decimal degrees.
code: # East Africa bounding box ag5_download(   variable  = "2m_temperature",   statistic = "24_hour_maximum",   year      = 2015,   month     = "all",   day       = "all",   area      = c(5, 28, -12, 42),   path      = "C:/agera5_data" )

title: Downloading AgERA5 data with ag5Tools

code: ag5_download(   variable  = "2m_temperature",   statistic = "24_hour_maximum",   year      = 2015,   month     = "all",   day       = "all",   area      = c(36.68, -3.37),   # lon, lat — Arusha, Tanzania   path      = "C:/agera5_data" )

title: Preparing APSIM meteorological files with ag5Tools
text: APSIM crop modelling platform requires site meteorological file containing daily weather observations specific variable names, units, header metadata. ag5_apsim() automates workflow: Extracts required AgERA5 variables locally downloaded .nc files. Applies unit conversions (Kelvin → °C, J/m²/day → MJ/m²/day). Computes site constants tav amp. Writes ready--use .met file (classic APSIM) .csv + constants file (APSIM Next Generation).

title: Preparing APSIM meteorological files with ag5Tools
text: maxt, mint, rain, radn four variables required APSIM simulations. wind, vp, rh optional used several crop modules.

title: Preparing APSIM meteorological files with ag5Tools
text: APSIM .met files carry two header constants derived weather record: tav — annual average temperature (°C), computed mean (maxt + mint) / 2 across days. amp — half range warmest coolest monthly mean temperatures (°C), computed (max(monthly_mean_temp) - min(monthly_mean_temp)) / 2. ag5_apsim() computes constants automatically extracted data.

title: Preparing APSIM meteorological files with ag5Tools
text: variables argument accepts three forms:

title: Preparing APSIM meteorological files with ag5Tools
text: filename = NULL (default), ag5_apsim() returns annotated data.frame prints site constants console.
code: library(ag5Tools)  met <- ag5_apsim(   coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),   # lon, lat — Arusha, Tanzania   start_date = "2015-01-01",   end_date   = "2015-12-31",   variables  = "required",   path       = "C:/agera5_data" )  head(met) #>   year day   maxt   mint  rain      radn #> 1 2015   1  27.43  17.89  0.00  19.42 #> 2 2015   2  28.12  18.03  0.00  20.11 #> 3 2015   3  26.78  17.61  2.34  15.73 #> ...  attr(met, "tav") attr(met, "amp")

title: Preparing APSIM meteorological files with ag5Tools
text: Set filename path without extension; ag5_apsim() appends .met. output file arusha_2015.met looks like:
code: ag5_apsim(   coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),   start_date = "2015-01-01",   end_date   = "2015-12-31",   path       = "C:/agera5_data",   filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2015",   format     = "classic" ) ! Generated by ag5Tools latitude = -3.37 (degrees) longitude = 36.68 (degrees) tav = 20.34 (oC) amp = 1.72 (oC)  year day radn maxt mint rain wind vp rh () () (MJ/m2) (oC) (oC) (mm) (m/s) (hPa) (%) 2015 1 19.42 27.43 17.89 0.00 2.3 18.4 71 2015 2 20.11 28.12 18.03 0.00 1.9 17.9 68 ...

title: AgERA5 covariates in PlackettLuce models
text: PlackettLuce models probability ranking outcomes widely used farmer-participatory variety trials using tricot approach. pltree() extends partitioning trial sites groups distinct variety preferences, using environmental variables splitting covariates. article demonstrates : Derive location date information tricot trial dataset. Extract AgERA5 growing-season weather covariates ag5_extract(). Use covariates pltree() model.

title: AgERA5 covariates in PlackettLuce models
code: library(ag5Tools) library(PlackettLuce)

title: AgERA5 covariates in PlackettLuce models
text: beans dataset PlackettLuce contains 842 tricot observations bean variety trial Nicaragua (2015–2016). row records three randomly assigned varieties farmer rated best worst. columns lon, lat, planting_date give us everything needed pull growing-season weather AgERA5 observation.
code: library(PlackettLuce) #> Warning: package 'PlackettLuce' was built under R version 4.5.3 data(beans) str(beans[, c("variety_a", "variety_b", "variety_c",               "best", "worst", "lon", "lat", "planting_date", "season")]) #> 'data.frame':    842 obs. of  9 variables: #>  $ variety_a    : chr  "BRT 103-182" "INTA Rojo" "INTA Ferroso" "INTA Centro Sur" ... #>  $ variety_b    : chr  "SJC 730-79" "INTA Centro Sur" "INTA Matagalpa" "INTA Rojo" ... #>  $ variety_c    : chr  "PM2 Don Rey" "INTA Sequia" "BRT 103-182" "ALS 0532-6" ... #>  $ best         : chr  "C" "B" "A" "B" ... #>  $ worst        : chr  "A" "A" "C" "C" ... #>  $ lon          : num  -85.7 -85.4 -85.4 -85.4 -85.4 ... #>  $ lat          : num  13.1 13.3 13.3 13.3 13.3 ... #>  $ planting_date: Date, format: "2015-12-18" "2015-12-18" ... #>  $ season       : Factor w/ 5 levels "Po - 15","Ap - 15",..: 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 ...

what: Step 1: Derive a date range for each observation
title: AgERA5 covariates in PlackettLuce models
text: Bean trials dataset run approximately 90 days. add end_date column planting_date + 90.
code: beans$end_date <- beans$planting_date + 90 range(beans$planting_date) #> [1] "2015-09-10" "2017-01-10" range(beans$end_date) #> [1] "2015-12-09" "2017-04-10"

title: AgERA5 covariates in PlackettLuce models
text: extract two growing-season covariates: Total rainfall — sum daily Precipitation-Flux (mm) growing season. Mean maximum temperature — mean daily Temperature-Air-2m (Max-24h, °C). ag5_extract() function accepts data.frame coords. need rename columns match expected default names (lon, lat, start_date, end_date), pass column names explicitly. download AgERA5 files Nicaragua extracting:
code: library(ag5Tools)  # Use explicit column names since beans uses 'planting_date' not 'start_date' precip_list <- ag5_extract(   coords     = beans,   lon        = "lon",   lat        = "lat",   start_date = "planting_date",   end_date   = "end_date",   variable   = "Precipitation-Flux",   path       = "C:/agera5_data" )  maxt_list <- ag5_extract(   coords     = beans,   lon        = "lon",   lat        = "lat",   start_date = "planting_date",   end_date   = "end_date",   variable   = "Temperature-Air-2m",   statistic  = "Max-24h",   celsius    = TRUE,   path       = "C:/agera5_data" )  # Aggregate daily series to trial-level covariates beans$total_rain <- sapply(precip_list, sum,  na.rm = TRUE) beans$mean_maxt  <- sapply(maxt_list,  mean, na.rm = TRUE) # Nicaragua bounding box: c(north, west, south, east) ag5_download(   variable  = "precipitation_flux",   year      = c(2015, 2016),   month     = "all",   day       = "all",   area      = c(15, -88, 11, -83),   path      = "C:/agera5_data" )  ag5_download(   variable  = "2m_temperature",   statistic = "24_hour_maximum",   year      = c(2015, 2016),   month     = "all",   day       = "all",   area      = c(15, -88, 11, -83),   path      = "C:/agera5_data" )

what: Step 3: Convert rankings to PlackettLuce format
title: AgERA5 covariates in PlackettLuce models
text: .rankings() converts tricot best/worst choices complete partial ranking matrix suitable PlackettLuce() pltree().
code: # Build a grouped_rankings object from the tricot best/worst format R <- rank_tricot(data      = beans,                  items     = c("variety_a", "variety_b", "variety_c"),                  input     = c("best", "worst"),                  group     = TRUE)

title: AgERA5 covariates in PlackettLuce models
text: pltree() uses environmental covariates partition trial sites. Terminal nodes meaningfully different worth estimates indicate variety performance depends growing conditions.
code: pl_tree <- pltree(R ~ total_rain + mean_maxt,                   data    = beans,                   minsize = 50)  print(pl_tree) plot(pl_tree)

what: Step 5: Inspect worth estimates by node
title: AgERA5 covariates in PlackettLuce models
text: itempar() returns worth (log-ability) variety within terminal node, revealing varieties perform best wetter hotter conditions.
code: itempar(pl_tree)

title: AgERA5 covariates in PlackettLuce models
text: workflow extends AgERA5 variable. covariates commonly used variety trial analyses:
code: radn_list <- ag5_extract(   coords     = beans,   lon        = "lon",   lat        = "lat",   start_date = "planting_date",   end_date   = "end_date",   variable   = "Solar-Radiation-Flux",   path       = "C:/agera5_data" )  beans$total_radn <- sapply(radn_list, sum, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6  # MJ/m²  pl_tree2 <- pltree(R ~ total_rain + mean_maxt + total_radn,                    data    = beans,                    minsize = 50) plot(pl_tree2)

title: End-to-end workflow: from CDS to crop model
text: article walks complete ag5Tools workflow: Download AgERA5 .nc files Copernicus Climate Data Store. Extract time series specific variables field trial locations. Prepare APSIM meteorological files crop simulation. example uses arusha_df dataset bundled package — 100 synthetic field trial plots Arusha region, Tanzania, planting harvest dates. four columns : lon, lat (decimal degrees, WGS84), start_date, end_date (YYYY-MM-DD character strings). match default argument names ag5_extract().

title: End-to-end workflow: from CDS to crop model
text: extracting, corresponding AgERA5 files must disk. Downloads organised variable year; downloading full year daily global data one variable takes minutes depending connection speed. area argument limits download bounding box interest. use rough bounding box covering Arusha region.
code: # Date range covered by arusha_df range(as.Date(arusha_df$start_date)) range(as.Date(arusha_df$end_date))  # Download precipitation for the relevant period ag5_download(   variable = "precipitation_flux",   year     = 2015,   month    = "all",   day      = "all",   area     = c(-2, 35, -4, 38),   # c(north, west, south, east)   path     = "C:/agera5_data" )  # Download daily maximum temperature ag5_download(   variable  = "2m_temperature",   statistic = "24_hour_maximum",   year      = 2015,   month     = "all",   day       = "all",   area      = c(-2, 35, -4, 38),   path      = "C:/agera5_data" )  # Download solar radiation ag5_download(   variable = "solar_radiation_flux",   year     = 2015,   month    = "all",   day      = "all",   area     = c(-2, 35, -4, 38),   path     = "C:/agera5_data" )

title: Extracting AgERA5 data with ag5Tools
text: agERA5 data downloaded Copernicus Climate Data Store NetCDF files format, file extension .nc. data provided daily observations file correspond day. instance, want precipitation data year 2010, 365 files (366 case leap year). case want use precipitation data model covariates, seek specific dates extract data corresponding locations trial established. Instead, can use ag5_extract function demostrated next section. Let’s say observations field trials trait interest (e.g., yield) want link rainfall data explore effect rainfall trait. know plating harvest dates trial plot. can extract time series daily rainfall starting plating date finishing harvest date. synthetic example data shows dates random locations Arusha, Tanzania. ag5_extract() function can extract required data, long downloaded already. Notice data.frame arusha_df already column names match default arguments function. match, indicate column names arguments function ag5_download(). example, data.frame location columns named x y dates named planting_date harvest_date, call function ag5_extract() look like: Notice need worry providing specific folder files located, root folder know files . instance, stored AgERA5 data files folder D:/agera5_data/, also sub-folders precipitation temperature data, required specify path argument. case, providing path D:/agera5_data/ suffice.
code: data("arusha_df", package = "ag5Tools")  head(arusha_df) #>        lon       lat start_date   end_date #> 1 35.72636 -2.197162 1991-04-22 1991-08-20 #> 2 36.10249 -2.850983 1990-01-24 1990-05-24 #> 3 35.46292 -3.602582 1991-03-06 1991-07-04 #> 4 36.29166 -3.855945 1990-10-10 1991-02-07 #> 5 35.45254 -3.616361 1990-01-22 1990-05-22 #> 6 35.40131 -3.216106 1990-10-19 1991-02-16 library(ag5Tools)  arusha_rainfall <- ag5_extract(coords = arusha_df,                                variable = "Precipitation-Flux",                                path = "D:/agera5_data/") arusha_rainfall <- ag5_extract(coords = example_df,                                lon = "x",                                lat = "y",                                start_date = "planting_date",                                end_date = "harvest_date",                                variable = "Precipitation-Flux",                                path = "D:/agera5_data/")
